name: Royal Mansour Marrakech
positioning: Palace hotel in the Marrakech medina, a few steps from Jemaa El Fna, where guests stay in private riads instead of rooms
best_for: Travelers who want a private riad with a personal butler in central Marrakech
Families, with a kids' club in Le Jardin de Lila

facts.text: The hotel is just a few steps from Jemaa El Fna square.
The estate covers 5 hectares, protected by the walls of the imperial city and overlooked by the Atlas Mountains.
Each riad is unique and decorated in its own style.
The private riads have one to four bedrooms and a pool.
Riads have lounges, shaded patios and terraces with a view of the Atlas Mountains.
The hotel has four signature restaurants.
La Grande Table Marocaine is the hotel's fine dining restaurant.
The spa has a hammam, a hairdressing salon, a gym, a heated swimming pool and an atrium.
The kids' club is in Le Jardin de Lila.
The hotel offers cooking, patisserie and mixology workshops.
The hotel is owned by the King of Morocco.

highlights.text: The hotel is designed as a medina within a medina: riads replace rooms and suites, and winding alleyways replace corridors.
Each riad opens through its own private entry courtyard with a fountain, and every riad comes with 24/7 access to a personal butler.
A network of hidden tunnels and elevators lets staff serve guests discreetly.
Le Jardin, with its swimming pool, was designed by Spanish landscape architect Luis Vallejo.
The hotel offers an exclusive excursion to the nearby home of the late perfumer Serge Lutens, which is not open to the public.

considerations.text: The hotel sits close to the busy Medina and Jemaa El Fna square, though its layout makes it feel like a private estate.
Each riad is a three-story accommodation.
